method: built-in image_gen with original block-bee character study and rasterized region-planning diagram
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create an original simple black-and-white children's coloring-book page, portrait 2:3. Image 1 is the original WeightPlay block bee character identity: retain its cheerful square face, cuboid forelock, two cube-tip antennae, distinct three-segment bee body with bands, two wings and the single rectangular gardener satchel with the leaf badge. Image 2 is ONLY a spatial planning diagram, not artwork: use the sizes, separations and positions of its 27 large colored envelopes as a guide to place a bee above a five-petal flower, with six large feet and a broad safe margin. Do not reproduce any diagram text, dashed lines, colors, boxes as standalone objects, or the diagram's disconnected look: the result must be one coherent friendly bee with attached block limbs and wings. Unlike a detailed voxel render, simplify each element to one or two broad closed surfaces; six feet are individually separated by clear white gaps and each foot is a large easy fill target. The satchel is a single large attached rectangular form entirely within its wide body segment, with one generously sized simple leaf emblem; it must not overlap legs or wings. Body uses three large joined box segments, with two bold black bee bands. Use a large square face with friendly eyes and smile; eyes and their highlights are non-fillable facial details. The flower has five broad closed petals, a broad centre, a stem and two broad leaves; no overlap with bee. Leave a clear minimum gap approximately 8% of the page width between every subject contour and the enclosing page border. Large closed interiors, bold continuous black outlines on clean white paper; no gray, shadows, textures, hatching, gradient, color, added objects, labels, text, watermark, disconnected anatomy or tiny fill cells. Preserve original character personality while greatly simplifying its small voxel seams into large surfaces.
remaining: Independent source Art review; actual margin, closure and region analysis; production mask; 13 locale and mobile rendering/interaction verification.
